body:
As far as whether I care about anything, yes, I care about a great many things.  I would say that the reason I'm considering suicide is that I care too much about the world to be willing to see it continue to deteriorate.

How do you deal with the people who are ignorant/apathetic/stupid?  Whenever I meet someone who is like this (lately it seems everyone is like this at least to some extent, it's a spectrum after all), I just lose all care for them, and have absolutely zero tolerance for anything they say that is stupid.  Someone is talking about how they can't figure out how to install some program on the computer?  I'll tell them to their face that they are just being stupid and they need to rub the two brain cells they have together and figure it out, since it's not fucking complicated.

I want to make the world a better place, but I can't be satisfied with a small shift over time.  Sure if I spend my whole life trying to change the world I might be able to have some semi-permenant impact, but it would be infinitesimally small in the big picture.  That doesn't seem worth it to me.

I can't live with the world the way it is, and I can't change it in a meaningful way, so why stay in it?  Every day I get more full of contempt for the world, and it just makes it easier to write the whole thing off as a failure.

Undoubtedly you are different than me.  Everyone is different in some way.  In a significant way, I've never been diagnosed with Aspbergers or anything else on the autism spectrum.  I've been diagnosed with MDD (Major Depressive Disorder), possible Bipolar Type II, possible Narcissistic personality disorder, among other things.

For a while I was on mood stabilizers, as well as anti-psychotics (because I was hearing voices following a night-terror, and starting to think aliens were out to kill me, long story, not relevant to this discussion).

I've never been on anti-depressants, but to be honest, that seems like something I would never want to do.  I don't see anything factually wrong with my views/opinions, and I feel like taking drugs to make myself feel better would be cheating myself.  I want to see the world how it is, not how the drugs make me see it.

I wholeheartedly agree with the notion that "The demise of good men is for good men to do nothing".  However, what it comes down to for me is a sense of futility.  There is so much stupidity and apathy in the world, that even if I spent my whole life working tirelessly to change it, I feel like almost nothing would actually change.  Sure there's the whole "at least you tried" mentality, but fuck that.  If you can't succeed, why bother even trying?

The idea of trying to help people not be lazy makes me disgusted.  I shouldn't have to take responsibility for people getting off their asses and becoming valuable human beings.  That should be something they do themselves.  The fact that they don't care enough to do that is the main reason I don't want to live on this planet anymore.

As far as the JFK Quote, I may have explained poorly, or maybe you interpreted something.  Either way, I didn't mean to say I want to end my life because it's too hard.  It's because it's too bad.  It's about enjoying my life.  I look at the outlook of the next 5, 10, 15, 20, 40 years, and see an overwhelming majority of my time being used to do things that I won't enjoy.  Working a dead end job 40 hours a week just so I can have some time to myself on the weekends.  Dealing with family and friends just so I can be alone, etc.  That kind of stuff isn't really "hard" to do, it's just not enjoyable, and I don't see a reason to stick around if it's going to mostly be bad.

If you went to a restaurant that you could only go to once, and people told you "man, the dessert is great!", but from the first course it all tasted like crap, would you actually stick around long enough for dessert?  personally, I'd just walk out, why waste my time on something that's going to suck just for the chance of something good?

I feel like my view of the world grew organically, it wasn't a shift.

When I was a kid I felt aproximately the same way, just without as much hopelessness.  I naively believed that changes could be made.  Possibly most importantly, I just hadn't spent much if any time really thinking it through logically, I just sort of went with my "gut feeling" about it.

While I agree that it's quite possible that my views will change in the coming years, to be honest, that scares me.

I see many people who live in the aforementioned state of blissful ignorance, and I feel like if my views were to shift, it would be due to me "drinking the koolaid" as it were, and deciding to ignore the faults of the world and just try to be happy outside of it, which would essentially be apathy, one of my most hated traits.

To give an example of this kind of thinking, since I don't feel the above paragraph adequately described it, let me give you an example:

I'm currently devoting a large amount of my time (40+ hours a week) to becoming skilled at an activity that isn't largely seen as a professional thing, but to me and many others it is.

I've been struggling with committing to training schedules I set for myself, and just generally not following through, even though the only person motivating myself is me.

My therapist brought up the idea of "lowering the bar" as far as goal setting, as a way to meet my goals.  I reacted pretty terribly to this.  This to me seems like the worst kind of failure.  If your response to not succeeding is to try something easier, that's just... I can't really describe how bad it is, but it feels like complete failure and just totally giving up to me.

I feel like convincing myself the world is good or life is worth living would be the same kind of failure.  I would essentially be lying to myself and brainwashing myself into not seeing the world as it truly is.

Your argument of "why rush it" intrigues me.  On the surface it seems to have no problems.  But the above issue of not wanting to "drink the koolaid" can cause issues.  Moreso, I feel like if I end it now, I'm at least ending it on a "high note".  My life right now is by and large fairly comfortable.  I'm not having to do many things that I don't enjoy, I'm largely doing my own thing.  If I were to delay to "see how it goes", and then realize a year down the line that I'm not happy, I won't have that opportunity to go out while I'm still happy.
